statement: For jointly Gaussian x = [x1; x2] ~ N(μ, Σ) with x1 of size q×1, x2 of size (N-q)×1, μ = [μ1; μ2], Σ = [[Σ11, Σ12], [Σ21, Σ22]], the conditional distribution of x1 given x2 = a is Gaussian: (x1 | x2 = a) ~ N(μ̄, Σ̄), where μ̄ = μ1 + Σ12 Σ22^{-1} (a - μ2) and Σ̄ = Σ11 - Σ12 Σ22^{-1} Σ21, the Schur complement of Σ22 in Σ.

symbols.meaning: N-dimensional jointly Gaussian random vector, partitioned [x1; x2]
covariance of x, partitioned into blocks

symbols.dimensions: q x q, q x (N-q), (N-q) x q, (N-q) x (N-q)

symbols.meaning: auxiliary variable x1 - Σ12 Σ22^{-1} x2, shown independent of x2
mean of the conditional distribution x1 | x2 = a
covariance of the conditional distribution x1 | x2 = a; Schur complement of Σ22 in Σ

steps.text: Partition the jointly Gaussian vector x = [x1; x2] (sizes q x 1 and (N-q) x 1) with mean μ = [μ1; μ2] and covariance Σ = [[Σ11, Σ12], [Σ21, Σ22]] accordingly.

Define the auxiliary variable y1 = x1 - Σ12 Σ22^{-1} x2. This is an affine transformation [x2; y1] = B x + c with B = [[0, I], [I, -Σ12 Σ22^{-1}]], c = 0, so by the affine transformation property (Y = c + BX ⟹ Y ~ N(c + Bμ, B Σ B^T)) the pair (x2, y1) is itself jointly Gaussian.

The source states directly that x2 and y1 = x1 - Σ12 Σ22^{-1} x2 are independent random vectors. Since (x2, y1) is jointly Gaussian (step 2) and, per the source, 'if a random vector has a multivariate normal distribution then any two or more of its components that are uncorrelated are independent,' this independence follows from cov(y1, x2) = 0.
Because y1 is independent of x2, its distribution conditional on x2 = a equals its unconditional (marginal) distribution: (y1 | x2 = a) ~ N(E[y1], cov(y1)), regardless of the value a.

Apply the affine transformation moments Y = c + BX ⟹ E[Y] = c + Bμ, cov(Y) = B Σ B^T to y1 = x1 - Σ12 Σ22^{-1} x2: this gives E[y1] = μ1 - Σ12 Σ22^{-1} μ2 and cov(y1) = Σ11 - Σ12 Σ22^{-1} Σ21 (the cross terms cancel using Σ21 = Σ12^T).

Since x1 = y1 + Σ12 Σ22^{-1} x2, condition on x2 = a: x1 | x2=a = (y1 | x2=a) + Σ12 Σ22^{-1} a. Substituting the distribution of y1 | x2=a from steps 4-5 gives (x1 | x2=a) ~ N(μ1 - Σ12 Σ22^{-1} μ2 + Σ12 Σ22^{-1} a, Σ11 - Σ12 Σ22^{-1} Σ21) = N(μ1 + Σ12 Σ22^{-1}(a - μ2), Σ̄).

The source identifies Σ̄ = Σ11 - Σ12 Σ22^{-1} Σ21 as the Schur complement of Σ22 in Σ, equivalently obtainable by inverting Σ, dropping the rows/columns corresponding to the conditioned-upon variables, and inverting back.

assumptions.assumption: x = [x1; x2] is jointly (not merely marginally) multivariate Gaussian.
assumptions.breaks_when: x1 and x2 are each Gaussian individually but not jointly Gaussian, as the source notes is possible (e.g. Y = X or -X depending on |X| vs c); the conditional-Gaussian result does not apply.
Σ22 is singular; the source notes Σ22^{-1} must then be taken as the generalized (pseudo-)inverse.

failure_modes.mode: Applying the formula to marginally-but-not-jointly Gaussian variables
failure_modes.signature: Conditional mean/variance computed from the formula do not match the true conditional distribution, which may not even be Gaussian.
failure_modes.cause: The derivation (steps 2-6) relies on (x1,x2) being jointly Gaussian so that uncorrelated implies independent and affine images stay Gaussian; this fails for non-jointly-Gaussian pairs.

failure_modes.signature: Σ22^{-1} does not exist in the ordinary sense; naive inversion is undefined or numerically unstable.
failure_modes.cause: Perfectly correlated or redundant components in x2 make Σ22 rank-deficient, requiring the generalized inverse as noted in the source.
